title: Introduce tool-call simulator and structured-output linting quickstart
author: Maya Patel
description:
This PR adds a self-contained quickstart demonstrating a local tool-call simulator and a lightweight structured-output linter for RAG/agent workflows. Motivation: teams often struggle to test tool-calling in isolation and to validate that agent responses match expected JSON schemas. This quickstart provides: 1) a small Node-based simulator that emulates external connectors (HTTP/webhook, SQL, and file-store) with controllable latency and failure modes; 2) an instrumented agent harness that exercises streaming tool calls and collects invocation traces; 3) a pluggable structured-output linter (YAML+JSON) that validates model outputs against declarative schemas and surface human-friendly error messages; 4) authoring guidance and a reproducible devcontainer for live debugging.

Checklist:
- [x] scaffold simulator runtime and README
- [x] add example agent templates (TS) and durable session playground
- [x] add structured-output linter rules and example schemas
- [x] wire CI smoke test for local simulator
- [x] add docs site snippet and quickstart landing page

Usage notes: `npm run start:sim` launches the simulator on localhost:8088. The agent harness uses the Redwood SDK sample config and a toggled `SIMULATOR_MODE=true` env var to route outgoing tool calls to the local simulator. The linter runs as a post-generation step and fails the quickstart CI if top-level schema mismatches are detected. This quickstart is intentionally minimal — it favors clarity over coverage and is intended as a tutorial/kit rather than a production-ready connector.
